title: asymmetric-throttle-pingburst-diary-jayden
content:
Purpose:
Quick scratchpad for the asymmetric throttle / pingburst experiment series. Trying to capture the run plan, raw observations, and next actions while it’s still fresh. This is a messy lab note; expect TODOs and shorthand.

Summary (one-liner):
We observed a persistent p99 spike when alternating high-frequency microbursts with long idle gaps under an asymmetric throttle policy. Warm-cache helps p50/p95 but p99 remains elevated due to preemption + cold-KV-cache refill.

Hypothesis: 
- Asymmetric throttle (aggressive preempt on low-priority lane during idle) evicts useful KV cache periodically, causing long tail on first tokens of bursty requests.
- Preempt + kernel warmup (cuda kernels) creates compound cold penalties for microbursts.

Environment / setup:
- Model: llama-variant-13b-fp16 (quantized to 4-bit in some runs)
- Runtime: redwood-runtime v0.19.2 (local dev cluster)
- HW: 1x A100-40GB, driver 535.86, CUDA 12.1
- Serving config:  max_concurrency=16; per-request priority lanes: high/low; asymmetric throttle: low-lane preempt_threshold=60s, eviction-policy=aggressive
- Batching: continuous batching enabled; batch_timeout_ms=10 or 30 (varied)
- KV cache: per-model local cache (capacity ~ 6GB), eviction LRU-like but with lane-weight adjustments
- Arrival pattern: custom pingburst generator (python) — pattern = [idle 45s, 6 bursts of 50 req/s for 3s each, 10s gap between each microburst]. Payloads small (avg 30 tokens). Duration 20 minutes per run.

Metrics collected:
- latencies: p50/p90/p95/p99, tail-heap (99.9)
- throughput: tokens/s and req/s
- kv_cache: hit-rate (prefix / token-level), eviction count per minute
- system: GPU util, memcpy stalls, kernel launch time distribution

Representative run (warm cache vs cold after long idle):
CSV snippet (run A = aggressive eviction, run B = conservative eviction):

run,phase,p50_ms,p95_ms,p99_ms,kv_hit,reqs
A,burst-1,32,78,420,0.63,290
A,burst-2,30,81,450,0.59,300
A,burst-3,28,74,510,0.52,305
B,burst-1,34,76,120,0.88,295
B,burst-2,33,79,130,0.85,298
B,burst-3,31,75,125,0.86,302

Notes on the numbers:
- Run A shows p99s in 400–500ms range during later bursts; kv_hit steadily drops across bursts (evictions happening between bursts).
- Run B with conservative eviction keeps kv_hit ~85% and p99 ~120–130ms stable.

Trace observations (stack sampling & kernel logs):
- High p99 traces show: stalled on KV fetch (host->device memcpy) + a few kernel cold-launch events immediately after preemption.
- Many p99 traces include a ~200ms host-side wait (scheduling + stall) before GPU work starts.

Quick ASCII chart (p99 over time, simplified):
Time -> |---burst1---|---burst2---|---burst3---|
RunA p99 -> 420ms -> 450ms -> 510ms
RunB p99 -> 120ms -> 130ms -> 125ms

Qualitative observations: 
- Warm-cache effect: first burst after long idle is always worse. If gaps <15s p99 stabilizes. The current aggressive preempt threshold (60s) means useful entries get evicted during the long idle windows.
- Batching/timeout: increasing batch_timeout_ms to 30ms reduced p50 slightly but had no impact on p99 spikes triggered by cache misses.
- Quantized vs fp16: 4-bit runs show similar relative patterns; absolute p99 slightly lower (fewer GPU ops) but still dominated by host->device and scheduling penalty.
- Preemption behavior: we’re seeing lane-switching cost that is not purely GPU compute — kernel context setup + KV rehydration cost is dominant.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Is eviction aggressive because of absolute memory cap or because lane-weighted eviction favors short-lived low-lane entries? Check eviction logs + make an instrumentation flag to tag entries by lane and age.
- Replay with pinned memory for KV buffers to measure host->device memcpy delta.
- Run with no preemption (disable lane preempt) as a control to isolate preempt vs eviction.
- Measure cold kernel launch cost in isolation (microbenchmark launching same kernels repeatedly).
- Try a tiny on-disk vs in-GPU cache to see if miss penalty changes ordering.

Quick next-run plan (priority order):
1) Instrument eviction logs to include lane tag + sequence id (GH PR quick change). (2d)
2) Control run: disable preemption for low lane, run same pingburst pattern (1d)
3) Pinned-mem experiment: allocate KV buffers pinned and repeat (1d)
4) Kernel microbenchmark for launch cost (0.5d)

Potential mitigation ideas (sketch):
- Short-term: raise preempt_threshold to 120s for low-priority lane if expected idle windows >30s, or switch to time-windowed eviction that preserves hot prefixes for x minutes after last access.
- Mid-term: *lazy rehydrate* — keep lightweight pointer info on host, only copy full KV pages on demand with async prefetch triggered at ~50ms into burst.
- Long-term: policy aware eviction that weights prefix reuse probability (derived from telemetry).

Random notes to self: 
- saw occasional OOM during a pinned-mem run last week — double-check accounting (might be double counted across worker threads).
- talk to SRE about kernel-launch queue depth logs (marta?).

Conclusions (draft):
Aggressive eviction + preemption under long idle windows explains the high p99 tails for microbursts. Simple policy tweaks (less aggressive eviction or longer preempt threshold) produce big wins; however, the root cause also includes host->device copy + kernel cold penalties that need targeted microbenchmarks to fully quantify.

Links / refs:
- GH PR: redwood/runtime#768 (eviction change branch)
- JIRA: INF-1123 (asymmetric-throttle investigation)
- Run artifacts: gs://perf-logs/asym-throttle/2025-04-18/*

End of scratchpad.
